verses.text: Jehoshaphat king of Judah came home safely to his palace in Jerusalem.
Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help wicked people and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, the LORD is angry with you.
But there is some good in you. You removed the Asherah poles from the land, and you have set your heart on seeking God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
He chose judges in the land, in each of the walled towns of Judah.
He said to the judges, "Be careful what you do, because you are not judging for people but for the LORD. He is with you when you make a decision.
So let the fear of the LORD be on you. Be careful what you do, because the LORD our God is never unfair. He does not take sides or take bribes."
In Jerusalem too, Jehoshaphat chose some Levites, priests, and family leaders of Israel to judge for the LORD and settle arguments. They lived in Jerusalem.
He gave them these orders: "You must serve faithfully and with your whole heart, in the fear of the LORD.

Your relatives who live in the towns will bring you cases about murder, or about laws, commands, rules, and decisions. In every case, you must warn them not to sin against the LORD. Otherwise his anger will come on you and on your relatives. Do this, and you will not be guilty.

Amariah the chief priest will be over you in everything that has to do with the LORD. Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the tribe of Judah, will be over you in everything that has to do with the king. The Levites will serve you as officers. Be brave and do your work, and may the LORD be with those who do what is good."
